subject: Arizona (Mike Candrea)
note: Titles 1991, 1993, 1994, 1996, 1997, 2001, 2006, 2007. Peak 1990s. Candrea retired 2021 as winningest coach in softball history (1,674 wins); 24 WCWS appearances. Best consecutive run = back-to-back (1993-94, 1996-97, 2006-07); never a 3-peat.

subject: UCLA (1988-1995)
finding: UCLA's peak run: dominant late-80s/early-90s core
note: 1988-90 three-peat went 163-19. Then 1992, and 1995 (vacated). UCLA is the all-time program leader (12 recognized). Best consecutive = 3-peat 1988-90.

subject: UCLA 1990
note: During a 22-game win streak (Mar 31-May 3) outscored opponents 68-3, including 122 straight scoreless innings over 13 games. 1990 title team.

subject: Washington (2009)
finding: Washington title era under Heather Tarr
note: Danielle Lawrie-led 2009 champions. Not a multi-title dynasty; single peak title. Frequent WCWS contender otherwise.

subject: Florida (Tim Walton)
note: Back-to-back 2014 and 2015. Florida also reached finals 2011, 2013, 2017, 2023. 2014-15 is the dynasty peak.

subject: Alabama (Patrick Murphy)
note: First SEC program to win a softball national title (2012). Perennial WCWS team (16 appearances) but single championship.

subject: Texas (Mike White)
finding: Texas recent rise: first titles 2025 + 2026 back-to-back
note: 2025 = program's FIRST national title; 2026 = repeat (def. Texas Tech 4-1). Teagan Kavan became first 2-time WCWS Most Outstanding Player (2025, 2026). Texas BEAT Oklahoma in the 2024 final series but lost; Texas won 2025 & 2026. Note: Texas did NOT win 2025 over OU's four-peat year - the four-peat ended 2024, then Texas won 2025.

subject: Oklahoma (Patty Gasso)
note: Titles 2000, 2013, 2016, 2017, 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024. 2016-17 back-to-back, then 2021-2024 FOUR-PEAT. Gasso's 8 titles tie Candrea for most by any D1 softball coach.

subject: Oklahoma 2021-2024
finding: FIRST four-peat in NCAA D1 softball history
source: soonersports.com 'FOUR PEAT COMPLETE' + Big 12 + Wikipedia + Yahoo
note: VERIFIED YES - unprecedented. No NCAA D1 softball program had ever won 4 consecutive titles. Prior max was 3 (UCLA 1988-90; OU itself 2021-23 tied that before extending to 4). Clinched June 6, 2024 def. Texas.

subject: Oklahoma 2021-2024
note: 2021: 56-4 | 2022: 59-3 | 2023: 61-1 | 2024: 59-7. (A widely-cited variant figure is 232-15; the Wikipedia season-by-season sums to 235-15.)

subject: Oklahoma 2022
finding: Argued most dominant single season in D1 softball history
note: 40 run-rule wins in 62 games (record); 38-0 start (NCAA record win streak to open a season); all 3 losses came to WCWS semifinalists (Texas, Oklahoma State, UCLA). Win% one point shy of UCLA 1992 but deemed more dominant.

subject: Oklahoma 2023
note: Only loss was Feb 4-3 to Baylor at a Waco tournament. Highest win% of the four-peat seasons.

subject: Oklahoma vs UCLA vs Arizona
note: Longest consecutive title streaks: Oklahoma 4 (2021-24); UCLA 3 (1988-90); Arizona best was back-to-back (never 3+). By consecutive-title peak, OU's four-peat is the greatest sustained run in the sport's history. UCLA still leads career total titles (12) and appearances (37).

subject: GOAT-coach tie
finding: Most national titles by a single D1 softball coach
note: Patty Gasso (Oklahoma) and Mike Candrea (Arizona) are tied at 8 each - the two winningest coaches by championships in the sport.
